issues.detail: The Hebrew 'וְתִשֶּׂנָה עָלֵינוּ נֶהִי' means 'and they (fem.) lift up a lament over us' (i.e., raise a wailing over us), not 'attack us' (攻擊我們). The verb נָשָׂא with נֶהִי means 'to lift up a lamentation', not 'to attack'. The Chinese '攻擊我們' introduces a hostile military action not present in the Hebrew, changing the meaning.
